title: Understanding the Learning Rate
text: The learning rate, often denoted as alpha, is a crucial parameter in gradient descent. It determines the size of the steps taken towards the minimum of the loss function.

title: Effects of a Large Learning Rate
text: If the learning rate is too large, what might happen to the gradient descent process?

title: Consequences of a Large Learning Rate
text: A large learning rate can cause the algorithm to overshoot the minimum, leading to divergence.

title: Effects of a Small Learning Rate
text: Consider what happens if the learning rate is too small. How does it affect the convergence of gradient descent?

title: Consequences of a Small Learning Rate
text: A small learning rate can make the convergence process very slow, potentially taking a long time to reach the minimum.

title: Optimal Learning Rate
text: The optimal learning rate balances the speed of convergence with the stability of the algorithm. It should be neither too large nor too small.
